answer: Sequential labor summit: each identity must complete a verifiable, uniquely-published compute task chain whose intermediate states are committed to a public log; registration requires solving the next unsolved link, so identities cannot batch-mint. Attacker cost is serial wall-clock time plus redundant compute, scaling linearly per identity. A jetty rule voids any chain sharing intermediate state hashes with another. Task difficulty is tuned via shale-like layered hash puzzles to keep first-solve latency near one hour.
